title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Verdant AI
summary: Intro discovery focused on PLG quickstart: free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs. Customer is evaluating Redwood for an internal search+assistant feature; primary concerns: latency for 100ms-500ms responses, cost control, data residency, SSO/KMS, and time-to-prod. Agreed next steps: send Quickstart guide, trial credits, security pack, and schedule a 1:1 benchmark session with their infra team.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Anna (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Anna from Redwood, I'm the AE for this account, with Sanjay our solutions engineer. quick intro?
[00:18] Jordan (CTO): Yeah Jordan here, CTO at Verdant AI. We build internal knowledge assistant and semantic search for our enterprise customers.
[00:32] Maya (ML Eng): Hi Maya, ML engineer, I'll own the model infra eval. Ethan and Sam are also on but they'll mostly listen.
[00:42] Sanjay (SE): Great, quick agenda, we'll do discovery, cover our PLG quickstart experience, free credits, and then dig into hosted vs dedicated vs private for your needs, any changes to that?
[00:55] Jordan: Sounds good. Our timeline is pretty aggressive; we want a smoke test in the next two weeks and a pilot within 6 weeks if things look good.
[01:05] Anna: Perfect. start with a couple qualification q's. what's your current stack?
[01:12] Maya: We're using OpenAI for assistant responses and embeddings right now; embeddings in Postgres via vector DB. Inference runs on a mix of cloud GPUs and some on-prem for regulated clients.
[01:26] Ethan: We also have strict egress controls for PII customers so anything leaving the VPC needs encryption and auditability.
[01:36] Sanjay: Got it. When you say strict egress, do you need a private deploy (VPC/on-prem) for the pilot or would hosted with VPC peering and strict retention work?
[01:48] Jordan: Ideally hosted for speed-to-value, but depends: if we can't get guaranteed region residency and KMS controls, we may have to do dedicated or private.
[02:02] Anna: For quickstarts, our hosted API gives immediate access — you can get tokens, SDKs, and be live in under an hour; we typically provide trial credits to run 100-200k tokens of testing. For region/KMS you can request private options or Dedicated reserved capacity.
[02:19] Sam (Product): Quick question on time-to-first-token — we measure developer onboarding time. How fast can a new engineer go from signup to a successful generation?
[02:30] Sanjay: With our Quickstart it's targeted under 30 minutes: signup, API key, SDK snippet, and a sample prompt. Streaming responses and examples are included. There are also Postman and curl examples.
[02:44] Maya: Are there sandbox limits for the trial? Rate limits?
[02:49] Anna: Yes, trial projects have soft quotas to prevent abuse, but we configure elevated trial quotas for customer pilots. We'll happy to open higher RPS for your benchmark window.
[02:59] Jordan: What about latency — we need tail latencies under 500ms for short prompts and about 100-200ms for embeddings lookups ideally.
[03:11] Sanjay: For embeddings and small prompt completions on hosted, typical p95 is 80-200ms depending on model choice and region. For ultra-low latency we recommend Dedicated with pinned GPUs and model variants. Also caching/prefix-KV can shave 30-50% of token cost and latency for repeated queries.
[03:31] Ethan: You mentioned caching — is that automatic? How is it controlled?
[03:36] Sanjay: It's automatic at the runtime layer for compatible routes; you can opt-in per model/route and set TTLs. We also do workload-aware batching to balance latency and throughput.
[03:50] Maya: Security: do you provide SOC 2, ISO? SSO? KMS integration?
[03:56] Anna: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO in progress; we support SSO/SAML, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. Hosted offers KMS-backed encryption and audit logs but not customer-managed keys unless you go Dedicated or Private.
[04:16] Jordan: How about data retention and logs? Some regulated clients need logs retained for 7 years or must be purged after 30 days.
[04:24] Lina (CSM): We can configure retention policies per account if you're on enterprise plans or Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted has configurable retention up to X days; for longer retention we can discuss an add-on.
[04:37] Sam: Any gotchas migrating from OpenAI to Redwood API?
[04:42] Sanjay: Our API is REST/SDK-first and designed to be drop-in for common patterns; we provide sample migration scripts for embeddings and prompt templates. The model catalog includes curated open models and verified performance profiles so you can pick a closest match. Occasionally tokenization differences affect prompt footprints — we'll help measure that.
[04:59] Maya: On the pilot side, what's a reasonable success criteria?
[05:03] Anna: We suggest: 1) Functionally parity on a set of 10 canonical prompts, 2) Latency within your SLOs (p95), 3) Cost per 1k tokens within a target delta, 4) Integration with your SSO and audit needs.
[05:17] Jordan: Budget? We might start with the free credits then move to a small reserved Dedicated pool if results are promising.
[05:26] Anna: We can provision trial credits and a short Dedicated burst for benchmarks. Pricing for Dedicated is subscription/reserved; we'll send ballpark numbers.
[05:36] Ethan: We need to run an on-prem trial for one sensitive client. How fast can Private deploy be provisioned?
[05:43] Sanjay: Private is heavier lift—typical lead times vary: for our packaged on-prem it can be weeks to months depending on their network and compliance. If you need immediate isolation, Dedicated in your region with customer-managed KMS can bridge the gap.
[05:58] Maya: Any specifics on model quantization or performance tuning? We run a mix of LLMs and smaller fine-tuned models.
[06:07] Sanjay: We support quantized model variants and our runtime picks kernels based on sequence distribution; we can recommend quantization profiles for your workload and do a quality/perf tradeoff analysis.
[06:20] Sam: Competitors question: are you seeing customers switch from OpenAI or other LLM APIs?
[06:26] Anna: Yes, many customers start with hosted OpenAI and move to Redwood for cost control, dedicated SLAs, or private deployment needs. Competitors mentioned often include OpenAI, Anthropic, and in some cases cloud-managed endpoints from major clouds.
[06:40] Jordan: Good to know. For the quickstart — can you walk us through the exact steps we should expect?
[06:46] Sanjay: Sure: 1) Sign up and create project, 2) get API key and install SDK, 3) run sample prompt and embeddings, 4) we'll enable trial credits and bump quotas, 5) run your canonical prompt suite and we'll assist with benchmark metrics capture. We can do a joint live benchmark where we stream results.
[07:10] Maya: We'll need to run an embedding migration test from OpenAI vectors to see delta.
[07:14] Sanjay: We'll provide a migration script and a notebook.
[07:18] Jordan: About observability — does Redwood Console show per-route cost and token breakdown?
[07:24] Lina: Yes console includes token-level cost, latency breakdown, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. You can export logs to your SIEM.
[07:36] Ethan: For the pilot network architecture—can we restrict egress, set IP allowlists?
[07:42] Anna: Hosted supports IP allowlisting and private networking features; for stricter requirements Dedicated or Private gives you VPC peering or on-prem control.
[07:53] Sam: Ok, can you also share an example of a benchmark we should run?
[07:57] Sanjay: We'll send a benchmark template: canonical prompts, concurrency patterns, and recommended models. We'll also help configure intelligent batching to match your latency goals.
[08:10] Maya: Any gotchas with streaming? We rely on streaming tokens to render UI progressively.
[08:16] Sanjay: Streaming is supported in hosted and Dedicated; Private depends on packaging but generally yes. Streaming latencies are dominated by first-byte and model compute. We recommend smaller response windows for UI render.
[08:32] Jordan: Great. Let's talk logistics and next steps.
[08:36] Anna: Proposed next steps: 1) We send Quickstart guide + trial credits + security pack, 2) schedule a 1-hour benchmark session with your infra and ML team next week, 3) set up a short Dedicated burst for a 48-hour benchmark if you want more consistent perf.
[08:57] Jordan: That works. For security pack, include SOC2 report, pen test summary, SAML docs, and KMS integration docs.
[09:08] Lina: We'll attach those to the follow-up email.
[09:12] Sam: Who will own the benchmark session on your side?
[09:16] Sanjay: Sanjay will lead the technical session and Anna will coordinate billing/trial. Lina will handle CSM and security artifacts.
[09:25] Maya: Expected outputs from our side: canonical prompt set, dataset sample, and a list of regulatory constraints per client.
[09:36] Anna: Perfect. Any final questions?
[09:40] Jordan: Not today. Thanks all.
[09:42] Anna: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite.
[09:46] END TRANSCRIPT (note: automated transcription quality medium; minor mis-hearings possible)
